headline: Advances in Quantum Protocols, Optics, and Control
summary: Today's selection bridges rigorous quantum information bounds with pragmatic physical device engineering. Theoretical work delivers deeper insights into one-shot entanglement distillation and random benchmarking noise structures, while software verification tackles QECC implementations. Complementing these, photonics advances range from nonlinear QED noise formulations to high-Q optomechanical metasurfaces and FPGA-stabilized laser feedback.

themes.title: Quantum Information & Verification
themes.body: Studies advance protocol efficiency and verification, from one-shot entanglement bounds and Markovian error characterization in RB to concolic testing for thousand-qubit QECC software.

themes.title: Precision Photonics & Optomechanics
themes.body: Hardware and theoretical optical advances establish high-reflectivity nanomechanical membranes, FPGA predictive feedback for laser stabilization, and non-Gaussian noise in nonlinear QED.

connections.body: Both 2610.31500 and 2610.31443 tackle error diagnosis in quantum architectures, contrasting analytical perturbation of physical noise in benchmarking against symbolic execution to locate software decoder bugs.
Both 2610.31452 and 2610.31396 address core bottlenecks in precision optical instrumentation, reducing phase and mechanical noise via engineered nanostructured metasurfaces and digital FPGA feedback.
